correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the five set-partition types of a product of four permutation sums give an exact bilinear expression R_n(u,v), and direct variance calculation gives E X²=1/(n-1) under unit coefficient norms. The critical zero-sum power-sum extremum is established by a three-coordinate constraint-circle argument, including exclusion of three-valued global extrema, followed by a two-level multiplicity optimization. The separately affine R_n has explicitly compared corner values, with strict uniqueness for n>=5 and balanced n=4; n=2,3 follow from direct identities. A standalone exact rational checker recomputed 136 direct permutation tests, 197 corner comparisons and 3157 two-level profiles. Finite tests are corroboration, not a proof over all n.

originality.rationale: The new claim optimizes the fourth moment over rank-one matrix coefficients of the symmetric-group standard representation with a complete n=2,3,4,>=5 equality classification. Barbour--Janson establish permutation-array CLT and second moment, not this optimization; Filmus et al. give global low-degree hypercontractivity, not this sharp coefficient theorem. A published co-singleton Fourier result does imply the separate zero-sum fourth-power bound, but does not imply the permutation fourth-moment formula (a distribution over n! points) or the balanced n=4 optimizer. Searches found no equivalent full rank-one statement; unindexed prior work remains a risk.
residual_risks: Older exact combinatorial permutation-statistics moment literature may give an equivalent rank-one extremal theorem under different terminology.
The 1979 skewness/kurtosis paper was not available as full text; it likely covers a nonnovel lemma, not established to cover the new permutation theorem.
The unrestricted first Fourier-block norm on S_n is not addressed and could differ substantially; no novelty inference is made from lack of coverage in one partition.

value.rationale: The invariant is the sharp normalized fourth moment of canonical rank-one standard-representation matrix coefficients on symmetric groups, a natural restricted hypercontractivity question for combinatorial permutation statistics. The theorem provides an all-dimensional exact constant and complete equality classification, with a genuine n=4 balanced versus n>=5 one-outlier switch. It does not rest its value on re-deriving the classical power-sum bound or on an unsupported claim about unrestricted first-degree harmonics.
